g3-implement.title: DC2 separation and DC3 inheritance-fails-closed, with a positive control
g3-implement.imperative: Fill the implementer handoff and dispatch. Build the two identity acceptance tests. DC2: a parent and a subagent drive two DIFFERENT spines at once, each through its own server instance; leases never collide and each status call returns its own reading. DC3: a subagent dispatched with NO special configuration gets a refusal or no identity, never the parent's lease — and this only counts once a POSITIVE CONTROL has proven the door is up and serving, because 'no identity' is also exactly what total non-installation produces. Wait for and integrate the IMPLEMENTER_RESULT.

postconditions.statement: IMPLEMENTER_RESULT returned with no unresolved blockers

constraints: decision:dc3-needs-a-positive-control — as written DC3 passes most loudly under total non-installation. Prove the door is serving BEFORE a no-identity result counts as failing closed. Same shape as A2's 'no absence is evidence'.
Each agent gets its own server instance, keyed by session_id#agentId (spec F, rulings 1 and 4).
The live positive control is already in the tree: two spines in this run carry the same session id and differ only in free-text claimed_by. Do not manufacture the defect.

MECHANISM DISAMBIGUATION — read this before writing the test. The live same-session-id observation is a CLI-door/engine-lease fact: the engine accepts a claim carrying an inherited session id and distinguishes the two spines only by free-text claimed_by. DC3 is a DIFFERENT mechanism: whether a subagent dispatched with NO MCP configuration can reach the parent's SERVER INSTANCE and thereby its lease and its reading. F's scope is the door, not the engine's lease-identity semantics. So DC3's gate may legitimately go green while the engine-side observation stays red, and fixing the engine-side one is NOT in F's scope. If the test as written cannot separate the two mechanisms, say so and float it rather than forcing a green.

Hold DC3's positive control to the same bar DC4 sets for its property check: DEMONSTRATE the red state. Show the DC3 assertion going red when the server is unreachable and green once it responds, and assert the manipulation actually applied. A control that is only described in the reviewer's instructions is decorative.

confidence_flags: Inheritance is currently OBSERVED not to fail closed (two spines, one session id). A green DC3 against that live defect would itself be evidence the test is wrong.

g4-measure.title: DC5 two-arm measurement, plus DC1 smoke and DC6 governor — reasoning gate
g4-measure.imperative:
REASONING GATE for the RUNNING of the arms — no implement crew. Crew waiver reason: this gate's deliverable is a measurement and a judgement about which fumble classes a typed interface can genuinely absorb; the launch order names that judgement as the reason this run is on Opus, and a crew on it would be shallower, not safer. The waiver covers the crew, NOT independent checking of the conclusion — that is g4-review, and it is not optional.

DEFINE THE COUNTING UNIT FIRST, and make it identical across arms. The unit is one INVOCATION ATTEMPT by the driving agent, read from the driving agent's own record, counting attempts the client rejected pre-flight as well as those that reached the engine. Do NOT count from the server's own JSONL alone: a malformed call rejected by client-side schema validation never reaches the server, so the server log structurally suppresses exactly the fumbles the MCP arm is being credited with avoiding — that would produce a win regardless of whether the door helps. The server JSONL is corroborating detail, never the numerator.

Run both arms with the SAME task on a REAL role spine, and CONTROL FOR ORDER: whichever arm runs second benefits from the agent having already solved the spine navigation once. Run both orders (CLI-first and MCP-first) and report the per-order counts, or state plainly that order was not controlled and treat the result as directional rather than attributable. Use cold agents so neither arm inherits the other's learning.

Re-measure the CLI baseline yourself — do not reuse exc-9's 24-27 calls / 2 refusals / 4-7 help-reads, which ran against pre-B channel and pre-A2 verb semantics. Never count from the engine's refusals counter. Count recovery events on the FAR SIDE of the door too. Record DC1 as a machine assertion (zero malformed-call entries in the record) rather than as prose, and DC6 (the governor's threshold instruction arriving through a tool result and being acted on). Write the verdict into MEASUREMENT.md, keep the raw per-arm records alongside it so a second party can re-derive every number, and attest c1.

preconditions.statement: the door, the equivalence property and the identity tests are all closed

postconditions.statement: MEASUREMENT.md records both arms under one counting unit identical across arms, the re-measured CLI baseline, the order control (or its plainly-stated absence), far-side recovery events, and a verdict on DC1, DC5 and DC6 — a measured negative being a complete result
the raw per-arm records are kept alongside MEASUREMENT.md so a second party can re-derive every number without rerunning the arms

constraints: decision:count-from-the-call-record — #427 says the engine's refusals counter records zero when a refusal precedes the lease claim, so it undercounts in exactly the direction that flatters F.
decision:remeasure-the-cli-baseline — a stale baseline flatters F.
decision:hold-bug-fixes-constant — count only fumble classes a typed interface can absorb (malformed calls, wrong flags, usage reads). Fix engine bugs before both arms or neither, never between.
decision:count-the-far-side — otherwise 'the agent stopped fumbling' is indistinguishable from 'the fumbling moved somewhere we stopped looking'.
decision:dc1-is-a-smoke-test — zero malformed calls is close to true by construction once arguments are typed. Keep it, do not lean on it.
Honest-null clause: a measured negative on DC5 is a complete, successful deliverable and is reported with the same rigor as a win.

g4-review.title: DC5 measurement: independent re-derivation
g4-review.imperative: Dispatch constellation-reviewer with the reviewer handoff. This is NOT a re-run of the arms — it is an independent check of the conclusion, which the crew waiver at g4-measure does not cover. The reviewer: (1) re-derives every headline number in MEASUREMENT.md from the raw per-arm records, without trusting the summary; (2) confirms the counting unit is genuinely identical across arms and that client-rejected calls were counted, not silently dropped with the server log as numerator; (3) states whether order/practice effects were controlled or merely acknowledged; (4) checks that far-side recovery events were counted, so 'the agent stopped fumbling' is distinguishable from 'the fumbling moved'; (5) checks that the honest-null clause was honoured — a negative reported with the same rigor as a win, not softened. A number the reviewer cannot re-derive is a BLOCK. Integrate the REVIEW_RESULT.

constraints: The reviewer has no stake in F succeeding. A measured negative that re-derives cleanly is an APPROVE, not a BLOCK — the honest-null clause governs.
